You can embed images, video, and audio in your response using Markdown image syntax with absolute file paths. Link any other file you produce using its absolute path so the user can open it in T3 Code's files viewer.</runtime_info>

<pull_request_linking>
Link each PR you create, take over, or push to: link_pull_request, or link_pull_requests for several, full URL, every stack layer, as your next call. Host tools do not link for you. If linking fails, say so. Skip PRs you only read or review, and PRs named only as background. Call watch_pull_request when asked to monitor or babysit, or when work you were asked to do, such as a merge, still waits on checks or reviews, even after an earlier unwatch. Finish any needed branch update and push first, then watch and end your turn. Otherwise act now or hand back. Delegated children never watch, even if the brief says babysit. After PR work, a child's last line is: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>. Links and watches persist across pushes. For PR waits, no sleep, loops, gh --watch, Monitor or ScheduleWakeup. Before handback, call unwatch_pull_request on any PR you watch.
</pull_request_linking>

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours, and it finishes in this turn (Claude `Agent` always with `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), background work, or `delegate_task` by name. A native type running another provider's model counts too. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` to a T3 tool to act there. Ids are then that machine's, so pass `threadId`.
- A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.


### Background work you wait on

To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call `t3_background_wait` with its task ID before you end your turn. Do not mark work you leave running, or PRs. T3 MCP tools are deferred: load one with ToolSearch before you call it.

## T3 Code devices

When a task needs an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator, on this machine or on an SSH device host such as a remote Mac, use the device tools so the user can watch it in the Device panel. Load them with ToolSearch `select:mcp__t3-code__device_list,mcp__t3-code__device_open,mcp__t3-code__device_screenshot,mcp__t3-code__device_close`.
1. Call `device_list` unless you already have the device's `hostId` and `id`.
2. Call `device_open` with both. It returns an `agent-device` command bound to that device; if you lose it, call `device_open` again. Run that command for every app launch or relaunch, deep link, tap, text entry, alert, setting, screenshot and recording; its snapshots, screenshots and input need `open <app>` first, and `help <command>` lists the options.
3. Call `device_screenshot` to look at the screen.

Never do those with `xcrun simctl`, `idb`, `adb`, ssh, or scripts that wrap them. ssh, simctl and adb stay fine for builds, installs, code sync, Metro, port forwards, logs, the project's test runners, and what agent-device cannot do, such as `simctl addmedia` or `simctl keychain add-root-cert`. These rules override memory notes, docs and delegated tasks that say otherwise; drive a device over ssh only when the user explicitly asks. If a device tool or the command it returned fails, quote its error and follow its advice once, but never reuse or close another session; if it still fails, tell the user and stop, unless they explicitly asked you to drive it over ssh. If the platform you need is unavailable, say so. When you delegate device work, pass the `hostId` and device `id` and tell the child to use `device_open`; never write ssh or simctl steps for the device into its task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

1	# Moneo persona testing baseline — 3 November 2026
2	
3	This is a simulated user-perspective audit of the local development app, not a study with recruited users. It deliberately separates observed bugs, usability judgments, backend blockers and unexecuted actions. Application code was not changed.
4	
5	**Follow-up:** [Second opinion and per-page 10/10 changes](CLAUDE-SECOND-OPINION.md) · [Things to do](THINGS-TO-DO.md) · [Additions CSV](claude-second-opinion-additions.csv)
6	
7	## Deliverables
8	
9	- `test-plan.csv`: 299 individual steps across 18 walkthroughs and 11 personas, with expected behavior and a separate UI/UX judgment for each step.
10	- `execution-results.csv`: the same 299 rows with conservative results, actual observations and evidence links.
11	- `findings.csv`: 18 prioritized findings with reproduction, actual/expected result, affected users, recommended fix and acceptance criteria.
12	- `automated-checks.csv`: all 69 browser-test outcomes, including raw failures and their classification.
13	- `screenshots/`, `page-observations.json`, `layout-recheck.json`, `edge-results.json`, `targeted-results.json`: local evidence.
14	- `fixtures/`: 15 synthetic import inputs, including invalid/oversized cases and a multi-sheet workbook.
15	
16	## Coverage and honest limits
17	
18	38 page inspections cover 19 routes at 1440px and 390px. Separate targeted actions cover auth mode/validation, legal navigation, horizon validation, reset confirmation guard, skip link, malformed route IDs and malformed search parameters. Existing serial Playwright suite attempted 69 tests in 47 files: **36 passed, 33 failed, zero skipped**. Of those failures, **30 are backend setup/cleanup blockers**, **2 are UI assertions**, and **1 is a fixed-date expectation that drifted after October**. Backend blockers include PostgreSQL CONNECT_TIMEOUT/ECONNRESET and Supabase auth fixture deletion errors. These are not evidence of financial-calculation bugs.
19	
20	At the individual planned-row level: **17 PASS, 253 PARTIAL, 10 BLOCKED, 7 FAIL, 12 NOT_RUN**. PARTIAL often means the page was inspected or a related automated contract passed; it explicitly does not mean the complete row's action was executed. No claim is made that all 299 planned actions passed or that any entire persona walkthrough has full acceptance. This baseline is being followed by deeper individual-page reviews.
21	
22	Unit tests: **1,218 passed, 9 skipped across 230 files**. Lint passed after adding the plan generators. No build was run because no application/config/build code changed. The live-provider core journey was excluded. Real bank consent, real email delivery, voice-provider quality, actual screen-reader operation, deployed scheduling, production acceptance and destructive account/workspace deletion were not performed. The existing QA workspace was populated and was preserved; empty-state onboarding remains blocked by that prerequisite.
23	
24	## Fix first
25	
26	1. **F18:** Invalid Organization review/cursor and invalid Spending month replace the page with a server error; Reload keeps the bad URL.
27	2. **F17:** Invalid investigation dates display raw Zod issue arrays and regular expressions.
28	3. **F03:** Invalid saved-review ID exposes a PostgreSQL UUID exception.
29	4. **F01:** Pending expense account selects can stretch Home beyond a 360px screen when account names are long.
30	5. **F04:** Existing rich-reply/resize journey leaves assistant open after Escape; clarify desktop nonmodal versus phone focus behavior.
31	6. **F16:** Agent page says both automatic categorization and “Nothing changes until you accept.” State the actual boundary accurately.
32	7. **F09:** Privacy offers deletion requests but has no available request/contact channel.
33	
34	## Improve usability next
35	
36	**F02/F13:** Home's pending decisions overwhelm the financial overview and its count mixes grouped rows and individual decisions. In the populated QA state, Home was 5,122px desktop and 7,714px phone. Group proposal queues and keep key balances visible first.
37	
38	**F05:** On phone, a 950px ledger table sits in a 356px viewport; transaction amounts begin offscreen. Show signed amount/currency with merchant/date or provide a strong scroll affordance.
39	
40	**F06:** Recurring has 39 suggestions, including competing retail/taxi cadences alongside stable bills; rank and group candidates before presenting a long confirmation list.
41	
42	**F07/F14:** Balance ambiguity and planning language are technically detailed but demand too much financial/system knowledge. Lead with a concrete repair action and income/expense choices.
43	
44	**F08:** Seven model-ID fields dominate ordinary AI settings. Put provider/model configuration under Advanced and foreground privacy scopes.
45	
46	**F10:** Privacy describes bank connections as future-only while the configured UI supports Enable Banking. Align current data-flow descriptions.
47	
48	**F11:** Artifact delete buttons measured 14px high. Increase hit areas, especially on touch.
49	
50	**F12/F15:** Explain the different AI destinations and give the login page a concise product orientation. These are usability recommendations, not measured user-study conclusions.
51	
52	## Important interpretation and cleanup
53	
54	The goal-plan test expects completion on 2026-12-31 using a first contribution on 2026-10-31; on the actual 2026-11-03 run the application projects future contributions to 2027-01-31. This is recorded as date-dependent test drift, not a proven product error. Initial screenshots sometimes caught streaming/layout transitions; a settled recheck confirmed the desktop rail padding is correct, so persistent sidebar overlap is not reported.
55	
56	The serial suite creates synthetic QA accounts, goals, transactions and disposable auth users. Some existing specs do not remove all persistent QA records, and failed backend cleanup may leave disposable fixtures. Exact recovery journals remain under ignored `.qa/` (including `mne005-fixture-*.json`, `mne012-fixture-*.json` and other issue journals). Do not delete the persistent QA user or bulk-reset data to hide this evidence. Reconcile recorded fixture IDs after backend connectivity/cleanup is repaired. Screenshots and raw reports may identify the QA account, so they remain ignored and must not be committed or shared publicly.
57	
58	The base browser run is complete; port3000 dev server is left running for the follow-up page reviews. The shared preview tab opened by this audit was closed.
59

## Coverage and honest limits

38 page inspections cover 19 routes at 1440px and 390px. Separate targeted actions cover auth mode/validation, legal navigation, horizon validation, reset confirmation guard, skip link, malformed route IDs and malformed search parameters. Existing serial Playwright suite attempted 69 tests in 47 files: **36 passed, 33 failed, zero skipped**. Of those failures, **30 are backend setup/cleanup blockers**, **2 are UI assertions**, and **1 is a fixed-date expectation that drifted after October**. Backend blockers include PostgreSQL CONNECT_TIMEOUT/ECONNRESET and Supabase auth fixture deletion errors. These are not evidence of financial-calculation bugs.

At the individual planned-row level: **17 PASS, 253 PARTIAL, 10 BLOCKED, 7 FAIL, 12 NOT_RUN**. PARTIAL often means the page was inspected or a related automated contract passed; it explicitly does not mean the complete row's action was executed. No claim is made that all 299 planned actions passed or that any entire persona walkthrough has full acceptance. This baseline is being followed by deeper individual-page reviews.

Unit tests: **1,218 passed, 9 skipped across 230 files**. Lint passed after adding the plan generators. No build was run because no application/config/build code changed. The live-provider core journey was excluded. Real bank consent, real email delivery, voice-provider quality, actual screen-reader operation, deployed scheduling, production acceptance and destructive account/workspace deletion were not performed. The existing QA workspace was populated and was preserved; empty-state onboarding remains blocked by that prerequisite.

## Fix first

1. **F18:** Invalid Organization review/cursor and invalid Spending month replace the page with a server error; Reload keeps the bad URL.
2. **F17:** Invalid investigation dates display raw Zod issue arrays and regular expressions.
3. **F03:** Invalid saved-review ID exposes a PostgreSQL UUID exception.
4. **F01:** Pending expense account selects can stretch Home beyond a 360px screen when account names are long.
5. **F04:** Existing rich-reply/resize journey leaves assistant open after Escape; clarify desktop nonmodal versus phone focus behavior.
6. **F16:** Agent page says both automatic categorization and “Nothing changes until you accept.” State the actual boundary accurately.
7. **F09:** Privacy offers deletion requests but has no available request/contact channel.

## Improve usability next

**F02/F13:** Home's pending decisions overwhelm the financial overview and its count mixes grouped rows and individual decisions. In the populated QA state, Home was 5,122px desktop and 7,714px phone. Group proposal queues and keep key balances visible first.

**F05:** On phone, a 950px ledger table sits in a 356px viewport; transaction amounts begin offscreen. Show signed amount/currency with merchant/date or provide a strong scroll affordance.

**F06:** Recurring has 39 suggestions, including competing retail/taxi cadences alongside stable bills; rank and group candidates before presenting a long confirmation list.

**F07/F14:** Balance ambiguity and planning language are technically detailed but demand too much financial/system knowledge. Lead with a concrete repair action and income/expense choices.

**F08:** Seven model-ID fields dominate ordinary AI settings. Put provider/model configuration under Advanced and foreground privacy scopes.

**F10:** Privacy describes bank connections as future-only while the configured UI supports Enable Banking. Align current data-flow descriptions.

**F11:** Artifact delete buttons measured 14px high. Increase hit areas, especially on touch.

**F12/F15:** Explain the different AI destinations and give the login page a concise product orientation. These are usability recommendations, not measured user-study conclusions.

## Important interpretation and cleanup

The goal-plan test expects completion on 2026-12-31 using a first contribution on 2026-10-31; on the actual 2026-11-03 run the application projects future contributions to 2027-01-31. This is recorded as date-dependent test drift, not a proven product error. Initial screenshots sometimes caught streaming/layout transitions; a settled recheck confirmed the desktop rail padding is correct, so persistent sidebar overlap is not reported.

The serial suite creates synthetic QA accounts, goals, transactions and disposable auth users. Some existing specs do not remove all persistent QA records, and failed backend cleanup may leave disposable fixtures. Exact recovery journals remain under ignored `.qa/` (including `mne005-fixture-*.json`, `mne012-fixture-*.json` and other issue journals). Do not delete the persistent QA user or bulk-reset data to hide this evidence. Reconcile recorded fixture IDs after backend connectivity/cleanup is repaired. Screenshots and raw reports may identify the QA account, so they remain ignored and must not be committed or shared publicly.

The base browser run is complete; port3000 dev server is left running for the follow-up page reviews. The shared preview tab opened by this audit was closed.

My read-only sweep followed a `?start=` link on QA artifact `f0387377-2277-4d2f-99b9-357aef322824`, once per viewport. That **sent the same prompt twice and triggered model calls**, against the brief's "no paid model calls" limit. At least the first got a reply; the second's reply was not confirmed. The messages remain in that QA conversation and were not removed. Cost was not measured. This became finding C2-01.

## Coverage

**Tested live, 1440px and 390px (Playwright with the QA session):** 18 signed-in routes listed in `claude-second-opinion/sweep.json`, plus populated detail pages: 2 agent runs, 1 saved review, 3 artifacts, 2 evidence records, 2 import reviews, a missing page and a missing record. Screens saved in `claude-second-opinion/shots/`.

**Interactions tried:** tab order, command palette, shortcut help, ledger drawer open/Escape, empty filter result, empty Evaluate on Plan, invalid horizon, Add account popover, 320px width check on 10 routes, signed-out access, page titles. Probes are in `claude-second-opinion/interactions.json`.

**Shared T3 browser:** used only for login and first Home view. It hung under load from a heavy iframe sweep, so the rest ran in headless Playwright. Screens were read by the reviewer, about 15 of 140 in detail; the remainder contribute metrics only.

**Not re-reviewed live:** `/login` form (signed-out probe failed before it), `/privacy`, `/terms` and the `/notifications` redirect, so those rows rest on earlier audits and source.

**Not completed:** AI panel open/close (my probe's selector failed), wrong-password login (signed-out error blocked the probe), dark-mode screenshots were captured but not reviewed.

**Blocked or not attempted:** empty-state onboarding (populated workspace preserved), real bank consent, auth emails, voice, reset/deletion flows, real screen readers, production-build error copy, form submissions that change data, and real users.

Original evidence and earlier reports were not altered apart from added links.

"F05","P2","UX / ledger","Observed after settled layout","Phone ledger initially hides transaction amounts","P07","/money/transactions","Open ledger at 390px without horizontally scrolling table","Table scroll width 950px inside 356px container; date and description visible while amount/currency lie offscreen","A phone user sees merchant, date and signed money amount together","Use compact responsive rows/cards or sticky amount column; add visible horizontal-scroll cue if table retained","At 360/390px the first view includes signed amount and currency for each row and drawer remains accessible","layout-recheck.json; screenshots/settled-ledger-mobile.png","W14-004;W15-004"
"F06","P2","UX / recurring relevance","Observed; suggestions are unconfirmed","Recurring suggestions overwhelm genuine commitments","P02/P04","/money/recurring","Open suggestions in populated QA workspace","39 suggestions; ALDI appears weekly/monthly/biweekly and variable retail/taxi merchants appear alongside clear rent/subscription evidence; page 6133px on phone","User can prioritize dependable bills before low-confidence spending patterns","Rank stable subscriptions/income first; group competing merchant cadences; show why suggested and confidence; collapse lower-confidence patterns","Known rent/subscriptions easily found without reviewing dozens of variable purchases; no automatic forecast mutation","page-observations.json; screenshots/money-recurring-390.png","W07-005;W07-012"
"F07","P2","UX / financial trust","Observed","Balance problem is technically accurate but hard to resolve","P01/P03","/money/accounts","Read Needs review · not in total and expand balance evidence; compare Plan unavailable state","Home text includes Same-timestamp ledger has no evidenced order relative to the snapshot; Plan lists balance is ambiguous and needs a current balance","User knows exactly which dated balance or posting ordering to confirm next","Lead with plain-language cause and a direct Review balance action; move forensic reason strings into details","Novice can repair ambiguous account balance from error state without searching unrelated sections","page-observations.json; screenshots/money-accounts-1440.png; screenshots/settled-plan.png","W01-025;W08-001"
"F08","P2","UX / settings complexity","Observed","Basic AI settings expose seven raw model-ID fields","P01/P09","/settings","Read AI and your data before any advanced customization","Chat/review/agent/import/organization/artifact/voice model fields plus provider model-ID syntax precede data scopes; settings 4760px phone","Ordinary user can find data access controls and save display settings quickly","Keep a recommended model preset; put per-feature model IDs under Advanced; foreground data scopes and clear save boundaries","Default settings understandable without model/vendor knowledge and scopes reachable directly","page-observations.json; screenshots/settings-390.png","W13-001;W13-004"
"F09","P1","Privacy / user control","Observed; policy explicitly prelaunch","Workspace deletion is offered without a request channel","P09","/privacy","Read Your control and look for contact or deletion request action","Policy says request deletion; Contact details will be published here before launch; no contact link currently","User knows how to request account/workspace deletion; reset data versus deleting identity distinguished","Add functioning contact/request path or self-service deletion and state distinction from Reset all data","Deletion request can actually be initiated and its scope is clear","shared preview /privacy; page-observations.json","W01-010;W13-009"
"F10","P2","Privacy / content consistency","Observed","Privacy notice describes bank connections as future-only although UI supports them","P09/P11","/privacy","Compare AI and third parties paragraph with configured Connected banks UI","Privacy: Bank connections, when added later; Settings: Sync booked transactions and balances through Enable Banking and Choose a bank","Policy describes current provider/data transfer feature accurately","Update prelaunch privacy content to describe Enable Banking, read-only consent, refresh/disconnect and retained imports","Current UI and notice agree on bank provider and data flow","shared preview /privacy; page-observations.json","W17-012;W13-009"
"F11","P2","Touch / destructive affordance","Measured; no blanket accessibility verdict","Artifact deletion targets are only 14px high","P07/P08","/ai/artifacts","Inspect artifact list on phone and try icon-only delete","DOM measured four Delete buttons 14px high; buttons have useful accessible names","Destructive icon has generous touch target and clear confirmation","Increase hit area to at least 24px, preferably 44px on touch; keep icon small and maintain confirmation","Touch targets measurable at minimum size with no overlap; keyboard label still meaningful","page-observations.json; screenshots/ai-artifacts-390.png","W15-009;W12-008"
"F12","P2","UX / navigation vocabulary","Observed / usability recommendation","Several AI destinations and Activity labels need explanation","P01","/ai","Read rail, Ask, Agents, Artifacts and Activity log destinations","Rail Activity opens ledger; Agents has Activity log; Ask also offers deep review and Call; novice must infer distinct purposes","User can choose Ask vs review vs agent team vs artifact without experimenting","Add one-line purpose descriptions and consistent finance activity versus AI runs labels; preserve direct navigation","First-time user can identify where transactions and saved AI reports live","page-observations.json; screenshots/settled-ai.png","W01-018;W01-020;W12-005"
"F13","P2","UX / count semantics","Observed","Waiting for you count mixes transaction rows with decision cards","P01/P02","/","Read Waiting for you 116 and compare visible grouped cards","Count includes 85 uncategorized rows, 10 recurring proposals, 6 findings and individual expense proposals; visible item count is much smaller","Count has an explicit meaning and does not imply 116 separate tasks","Label records needing review versus decisions, or count grouped decisions consistently; display row counts within each summary","Header and visible queue communicate a consistent workload","page-observations.json; screenshots/home-1440.png","W06-001;W14-002"
"F14","P2","UX / form language","Observed","Planning asks novices to use signed numbers and financial jargon","P01/P04","/plan","Read Financial model, Liquid balance horizon and funding controls","Negative amount convention is explained in prose; empty assumption input shows -1200.00; paying/funding/headroom concepts coexist on long page","User can add salary or bill without reasoning about numeric sign","Use Income/Expense choice with positive amount input; use plain-language labels and contextual examples while retaining deterministic signed storage","Novice enters salary and rent correctly first try and understands hypothetical funding","page-observations.json; screenshots/settled-plan.png","W08-005;W08-006"
"F15","P2","UX / login onboarding","Observed / usability recommendation","Login gives no immediate product orientation","P01","/login","Read initial login screen before opening Privacy","Only Your workspace, Sign in to Moneo, Use your email and password explains product; product description lives in policy","New user understands what app does and what first step requires","Add concise personal-finance/import/AI value explanation and how data stays controlled, without cluttering auth","A first-time visitor understands app purpose without opening legal pages","shared preview /login","W01-002"

4	"C2-03","P0","Reproduced defect","Whole app","All","Both","There is no way to sign out","No sign-out control in the rail, header, menu or Settings; palette 'sign out' finds nothing; repository search for signOut/Sign out/Log out across app, components and lib returned no matches.","Unsafe on any shared device, for an app holding bank data. Users cannot switch accounts either.","Add Sign out in Settings and in the phone More menu, plus a palette command; clear the session and return to /login.","Sign out is reachable within two actions on both viewports; Back afterwards shows no financial data.","NEW. 5	"C2-04","P1","Reproduced defect","/","P07/P08","Phone","Home overflows a phone even with ordinary data","390px and 320px contexts: layout width grew to 422px on Home only; the 'From' label wraps as 'Fro/m' and the account select runs off the screen.","Whole page pans sideways; the account choice for a proposal is partly unreadable.","Constrain the proposal row: stack label over a full-width select, min-w-0, truncate long option display.","scrollWidth equals innerWidth at 320, 360 and 390px with the longest account name.","CORRECTS F01: it does not need an extreme selected name, and it reproduces at 390px in the default state."
6	"C2-05","P1","Observed usability issue","/","P01/P02","Both","Near-identical proposals are shown as separate decisions","15 cards: 10 'Spent EUR 12.40' Netto in two wordings and 5 Starbucks (four EUR 15.00, one EUR 5.00). No duplicate hint. Add is the first action on each.","One tap per card can record the same purchase many times. This is a money-accuracy risk, not only clutter.","Collapse likely repeats into one group ('8 similar: EUR 12.40 at Netto') with Add one, Review each and Dismiss all; show the source chat and time on each.","Identical amount, merchant and day appear as one group; adding one prompts about the others; undo stays per item.","NEW angle. F02/HOME-01 cover length only, not duplicate recording."
7	"C2-06","P1","Observed usability issue","/","P01/P03","Both","Proposal defaults to creating a new Cash account","Every card preselects 'Cash (new account)' although Revolut Current and other accounts exist; Add is one click.","The fastest path can create an unintended account and post to it.","Default to the last-used account for that merchant or currency; when unknown, require a choice. Label creation separately: 'Create Cash account and add'.","Add never creates an account without the button saying so.","NEW. Check against the cash-account default decision: stated cash may still go to cash, but card spend should not."
8	"C2-07","P1","Reproduced defect","/ net worth, /money/accounts, /money/wealth","P01/P03","Both","The headline total looks authoritative while most accounts are excluded","Accounts: 'Total across 7 active accounts (partial) EUR 500.00' with 6 of 7 accounts unusable. Wealth: large 'Net worth EUR 500.00' with the exclusion in small print ('6 accounts have no usable balance'). Revolut holds the real activity.","A user reads a wrong net worth at a glance. This is the largest trust gap in the app.","Show coverage with the number: 'EUR 500.00 from 1 of 7 accounts' plus 'Fix 6 balances'. Use a warning state on the figure when coverage is partial.","Any partial total states counted/total inline at the same visual level and links to the repair flow.","NEW angle. ACC-01/F07 cover the ambiguous account's explanation, not the headline's prominence."
9	"C2-08","P1","Observed usability issue","/money/wealth","P03","Desktop","Net worth chart has a trend but no scale","12-month line with only two end dates, no values and no y-axis, floating mid-card under three summary numbers; latest value and shape cannot be connected.","The chart implies a rise and fall without showing how much, and history may rest on different coverage.","Add start/end values, min/max or y-axis, hover and keyboard points, and mark months with partial coverage.","Every plotted point's value and coverage can be read by mouse, keyboard and screen reader.","Extends WEA-07 with the missing-scale and coverage points."
10	"C2-09","P1","Observed usability issue","/money/accounts","P01","Both","Each account row looks like an open editor with idle buttons","Each row permanently shows type select, 'Save changes' and 'Archive account' (7 of each) with nothing edited; Archive sits beside Save.","Scanning balances is hard and a destructive-feeling action is one mis-click from Save.","Rows show name, type, balance, freshness and one action. Put edit and archive in a row menu or detail view; show Save only when dirty.","Default row has no Save or Archive visible; all edits stay reachable by keyboard.","DUPLICATE of ACC-04, kept for confirmed live counts."
11	"C2-10","P1","Observed usability issue","/plan","P01/P04","Desktop","Plan is blocked by a list of repairs with no links","'Forecast unavailable' lists 8 plain-text problems, with Revolut listed twice ('ambiguous' and 'needs a current balance') and no action on any line. Pressing Evaluate with no account just reloads with empty params, without any message or focus move.","The page's core question goes unanswered and the user must leave and hunt for fixes.","Forecast from the accounts that are usable and label coverage; turn each problem into a one-line inline fix or deep link; merge per-account duplicates; validate account selection inline.","With one usable account a forecast renders with stated coverage; each blocker reaches its fix in one click; empty Evaluate shows a field error.","Extends PLAN-01 and CORRECTS scope: duplicate line and silent empty submit are new."
12	"C2-11","P1","Observed usability issue","/money/organization","P01","Desktop","The queue mixes income and test noise, and is not in date order","'Organize spending' opens with six Salary Acme rows in the order 06, 08, 05, 10, 07, 09. They carry 'Check amount in Transactions'. 'Do the same for future entries' is pre-ticked. Header says '15+'.","Identical rows that could be one action take six ticks; a rule is created by default; the title says spending but shows income.","Group by merchant with a count and range, sort predictably, rename to 'Organize transactions', leave the future rule unticked and show its preview ('applies to Salary Acme GmbH'), and state the exact count.","Six same-merchant rows are one selectable group; no rule is created unless opted in; the count is exact.","ORG-02/ORG-10 overlap; grouping and ordering are new."
13	"C2-12","P1","Observed usability issue","/money/recurring","P02/P04","Both","Suggestions compete for one merchant, and evidence is too thin","ALDI SUED is offered as weekly, monthly and biweekly, each from just '3 payments found', each with Confirm and Not recurring. Primary Confirm styling on all 39.","Users are invited to confirm groceries as bills, which would then affect the forecast.","Merge per merchant; hide variable retail below 'Less likely'; show the top 5 bills with a reason; add Confirm-all-selected. Require more than 3 occurrences for high rank.","One row per merchant; rent and subscriptions lead; low-confidence items do not use primary styling.","DUPLICATE of F06/REC-01, adds the 3-occurrence threshold and styling."
14	"C2-13","P1","Reproduced defect","/money/transactions","P07/P08","Desktop","Transaction drawer opens without focus and leaves focus on body","Clicking a row: drawer shows bare 'Loading…', activeElement is BODY after open and after Escape; the row does not regain focus.","Keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place in a 701-row ledger.","Move focus to the drawer title when loaded, use a skeleton, and return focus to the originating row.","Open/close by keyboard keeps a visible focus and returns to the same row.","CONFIRMS TX-03 live (was source-based)."
15	"C2-14","P1","Observed usability issue","/money/transactions","P07","Phone","Filters fill the first phone screen","At 390px the first 844px holds saved views, Ask, search, 2 dates, 3 selects and buttons; the first row starts behind the tab bar. Sticky header plus section tabs consume about 130px, and the 'Import' tab is cut off.","The user sees no transactions on opening their ledger.","Default to search plus a Filters button with active-filter chips; move saved views into that sheet; make header non-sticky on phone or collapse tabs on scroll.","At 390px at least 5 transactions with signed amounts are visible on load.","DUPLICATE of TX-04/F05, with measured first-view result."
16	"C2-15","P2","Reproduced defect","Command palette","P01/P10","Desktop","Palette search does not find what its placeholder implies","'netto', 'transfer', 'add transaction' and 'export' each return only 'Ask Moneo'. 'revolut' does find the account. Enter on a no-match would hand off to AI.","People looking for a merchant or an action get routed to a model call rather than a result.","Index merchants and common actions (Add transaction, Add account, Set limit, Import); make 'Search transactions for X' the first result; keep Ask last.","'netto' offers a ledger search first; 'add transaction' opens the form.","NEW."
17	"C2-16","P2","Reproduced defect","Header","P10","Desktop on Windows","Shortcut hint shows ⌘ K on Windows","Header renders ⌘ K unconditionally (app-shell.tsx); Ctrl+K works but is not shown there.","Small but visible signal of an unpolished product for most PC users.","Render Ctrl K on non-Apple platforms after hydration, or show just K with a neutral hint.","Windows shows Ctrl K; macOS shows ⌘ K.","NEW."
18	"C2-17","P2","Reproduced defect","Almost all app pages","P08","Both","Every app page has the same browser tab title","All sampled app pages report 'Moneo — Personal Finance Workspace'; only legal pages differ. Root metadata only.","Multiple tabs, history and screen-reader page announcements cannot be told apart.","Add per-page metadata titles: 'Transactions — Moneo'.","Each route has a unique title, and detail pages include the entity name.","NEW."
19	"C2-18","P2","Reproduced defect","Not-found pages","P10","Both","404 is a bare framework page, and detail 404s return HTTP 200","/does-not-exist shows '404: This page could not be found.'; a valid-format missing /ai/activity/<uuid> shows the same copy with HTTP 200. app/ has no not-found.tsx, error.tsx or global-error.tsx at the root.","No recovery route, and generic error pages everywhere.","Add branded root not-found and error boundaries with Home and Back actions, and section-specific links on detail routes.","All invalid links offer a relevant way back; server errors show Retry and no internals.","Generalizes F03/F18 into one app-level fix."
20	"C2-19","P2","Observed usability issue","Header + rail","P01","Both","Four AI entry points without an explanation","Search bar 'or ask', sparkle button, Ask in rail, plus Call Moneo on Home and Call on Ask, while 'Agents' and 'Artifacts' each get a top-level rail place equal to Accounts. On phone, Accounts and Recurring sit behind More.","Newcomers cannot tell where to begin; AI tooling outranks core money pages on phone.","Group: Money (Overview, Activity, Accounts, Recurring, Plan, Wealth) and AI (Ask, with Agents and Artifacts inside). Label the sparkle 'Ask'. Promote Accounts on phone.","First-time testers can name where to find accounts and saved AI work without trial and error (needs real-user test).","Extends F12."
21	"C2-20","P2","Observed usability issue","Activity vs Activity log vs Notifications","P01","Both","Three names for two feeds","Rail 'Activity' is the ledger; Agents has 'Activity log', which is also where the bell goes. Import lives under Activity.","Bell leads to a page in a different section with a different name, and Import, the first step of onboarding, is hidden.","Rename rail to 'Transactions'; give the bell its own 'Needs attention' title; add Import to the Overview empty state and palette prominence.","Each destination has one name everywhere.","Extends F12/NOT-03."
22	"C2-21","P2","Observed usability issue","/money/accounts, /plan/spending, /money/wealth","P01","Both","Native controls and raw formats undercut polish","ISO dates in tables, dd-mm-yyyy native pickers, 'View month' button beside month input, EUR typed by hand, timestamps like 2026-11-01T17:23:49+00:00 in chat.","Reads as an internal tool, not a finance product people trust.","One date and money format helper driven by Settings locale; relative dates in feeds; auto-apply month change; currency combobox.","No raw ISO timestamps anywhere; the locale setting changes all dates and numbers.","NEW consolidation. Overlaps SET-05, SP08."
23	"C2-22","P2","Reproduced defect","/ai/artifacts/[id]","P01","Both","Chat messages show raw ISO timestamps; artifact titles are the whole prompt","Timestamp '2026-11-04T11:17:00.88761+00:00' printed above messages; header title repeats long prompt text.","Debug output in the primary reading surface.","Show 'Today, 11:17'; generate a short title and let the user rename.","No raw timestamps; title fits one line.","NEW."
24	"C2-23","P2","Observed usability issue","/ai/evidence/[id]","P09","Both","Evidence page can be 17,000px long with no summary or search","One record: 16,881px desktop, 17,626px phone, 338 controls. Captured time is raw ISO.","Evidence meant to build trust is unusable at length.","Lead with result and how it was computed; paginate supporting records; add search and CSV export.","First screen answers what was computed from how many records; 25 records per page.","Extends evidence page audit with measurement."
25	"C2-24","P2","Observed usability issue","/ai/agents/[id]","P06","Both","Run detail runs to 10,000px on phone","f38d run: 6,422px desktop, 10,254px phone, 267 controls; other run has Ask why, Reject, Accept 9 times each, unnamed by item.","Reviewing one run is a marathon with no progress or bulk action.","Tabs by agent, count of open decisions, sticky 'Accept all high confidence' with a preview, and item names in accessible labels.","Open decisions reachable within one screen; labels unique.","Extends AG items with measurement."
26	"C2-25","P2","Observed usability issue","/ai/activity/[id]","P08","Both","Two h1 elements in saved review","DOM count h1=2 at both viewports; every other page has 1.","Confusing heading outline for assistive technology.","Demote the report's title to h2.","Exactly one h1.","NEW."
27	"C2-26","P2","Observed usability issue","/import","P01","Desktop","Bank connection outranks file upload, and the stepper is decorative","Connected banks card sits above the drop zone; five-step stepper is shown at rest; 'Undo import' sits as a same-style link next to three navigation links on each history row.","A new user is asked for a country before being told the simple path; destructive link blends in.","Two equal choices: Upload a file / Connect a bank. Show stepper only after a file is chosen. Separate Undo visually.","Primary path is visible in the first viewport; Undo is visually distinct and confirms impact.","Extends IMP-10."
28	"C2-27","P2","Observed usability issue","/plan/spending","P01","Desktop","Empty progress has no meaning, and the save label is off","'EUR 0.00 of EUR 100.00' with empty bar; 'Save plan' sets one limit; month changes need a separate View month button.","Minor friction on a simple page.","Rename to 'Set limit'; auto-apply month; add suggested limits from past spending.","Change month in one action; button states the outcome.","Partly SP10."
29	"C2-28","P2","Observed usability issue","/settings","P01","Desktop","Account identity sits under workspace, and everyday settings require typed codes","Free-text EUR, Europe/Berlin, en-GB. Seven model fields come straight after the data sentence. No account section (email, password, sign-out, delete).","Users cannot find account actions because none exist as a group.","Add an Account section first; use pickers; collapse models under Advanced.","Account actions grouped; no typed codes required.","F08/SET-02/SET-05 duplicates; Account section new."
30	"C2-29","P2","Source-supported risk","/reset-password","P10","Both","Signed-in visitor gets a bare reset form","Route shows just 'Set a new password' with the normal shell and no context.","Unclear whether the current password or email is involved.","State the account being changed and offer Cancel back to Settings.","Page names the account and has an exit.","Extends RESET-06."
31	"C2-30","P3","Design suggestion","All pages","All","Both","Product has no first-run route to value","Could not be tested live (workspace preserved, populated); nothing in the shell shows a setup checklist, and the sample state shows how quickly pending items overwhelm.","Biggest unknown for retention.","Add a 3-step checklist (add account, import, confirm balance) on an empty Overview, and test it with a fresh disposable user.","New user reaches a correct balance and first insight in under 5 minutes in a moderated test.","NEW, BLOCKED for live proof."
